description: Linear headphone preference models: score = intercept - sum(weight * variable). Variables are computed on the error e = response - target on the evaluation grid (1/12 octave, docs/targets.md), with response (the left-right average) and target both normalised at 500 Hz. SD is the sample standard deviation of e (ddof = 1); AS is the absolute slope of the least-squares line of e against ln f (dB per neper of frequency); ME is the mean of |e|. Each variable states its band. 'training' is the fixture and target pair the model was fitted on; a score for any other pair is greyed out.

models.label: Harman around-ear and on-ear model (Olive, Welti and Khonsaripour 2018)
models.source: Coefficients: US patent application 2019/0087739 A1 (Harman International; S. E. Olive, T. S. Welti, O. Khonsaripour), 'Linear model to predict listener preference ratings of headphones', published 2019-03-21, Eq. (5) and Table 2 (RMSE 6.705); https://patents.google.com/patent/US20190087739A1/en. Model paper: Olive, Welti and Khonsaripour, 'A Statistical Model that Predicts Listeners' Preference Ratings of Around-Ear and On-Ear Headphones', AES 144th Convention, 2018, paper 9919, e-library 19436 (not read: paywalled). r = 0.86 and an error of 6.7 points are also stated in Olive, Acoustics Today 18(1), 2022, p. 65, which gives no coefficients.
notes: Band: the patent defines SD and AS from 20 Hz to 10 kHz for its variables. Erratum E7 and AutoEq (MIT licence, autoeq/frequency_response.py, harman_overear_preference_score, v4.1.2) use 50 Hz to 10 kHz for this model, AutoEq stating that its implementation reproduces Listen Inc.'s Excel template, which the model's authors supplied. This file follows E7; the primary paper was not available to settle it.
AutoEq uses the unrounded intercept 114.490443008238 and AS weight 15.5163857197367 (and 12.62 for SD). The rounded patent values used here differ from them by less than 0.01 points for |AS| below 2.
Grid: Listen's SoundCheck template expects R40 (1/12-octave) data from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, averages left and right and normalises at 500 Hz (Listen Inc. sequence note, archived 2023-03-27).

models.label: Harman in-ear model, patent coefficient set (US 2019/0087739 A1, Eq. 4)
models.source: US patent application 2019/0087739 A1 (above), Eq. (1)-(4) and Table 1; SD and AS from 20 Hz to 10 kHz, ME from 40 Hz to 10 kHz (paragraphs on Eq. 1-3 and claim 9). This is the set printed in the spec (Section 11); erratum E7.
notes: Model papers: Olive, Welti and Khonsaripour, 'A Statistical Model that Predicts Listeners' Preference Ratings of In-Ear Headphones', Parts 1 and 2, AES 143rd Convention, 2017, e-library 19237 and 19275 (not read: paywalled).

models.label: Harman in-ear model, coefficient set of Listen SoundCheck and AutoEq
models.source: AutoEq (J. Pasanen, MIT licence), autoeq/frequency_response.py, harman_inear_preference_score, v4.1.2 (https://github.com/jaakkopasanen/AutoEq), whose comment states that it reproduces Listen Inc.'s Excel template; erratum E7. ME is the mean |e| with e taken relative to its value at 500 Hz, which the 500 Hz normalisation of response and target already makes zero.
notes: No publication of this coefficient set was found; its fit statistics are unknown. The two in-ear sets differ by 10 to 30 points (E7), so a score always names its set.
